description: A non-interactive CLI for the Google Tag Manager API v2 (google-tag-manager-cli, command `gtmc`): look up containers by GTM-XXXX, audit and export them, edit tags, triggers, variables, folders, templates, clients and other entities in a workspace (also in bulk and from the Community Template Gallery), compile-check with quick-preview, create, stage and publish versions, and prove from a local audit log which accounts and containers were touched. Built for scripts and AI agents, with the complete reference embedded in the binary behind `gtmc llm`.
rules: Every edit happens in a workspace and is invisible to the site until a version is created from it (`gtmc version create`) and that version is published (`gtmc version publish <id> --yes`). Publishing changes the live site; get the user's approval first.
`gtmc version create` consumes the workspace — GTM deletes it. A new workspace is created only when it was the container's last one; otherwise run `gtmc workspace create --use` before editing again.
`--container` accepts a GTM-XXXX public ID without an account ID. Without `--workspace` the CLI uses the container's workspace only when exactly one exists; it never guesses between several.

`update --file` replaces the whole entity: start from the JSON of `get`. `create --file` drops IDs, paths and fingerprints but does not rewrite references (trigger IDs, folder IDs, {{variable}} names, cvt_ template types); use `workspace bulk-update` with new_N placeholder IDs to copy entities with their references.
A stale fingerprint fails with `400 The provided entity fingerprint is not valid.` (not 409): get the entity again and redo the edit.
Run `gtmc workspace quick-preview` before `version create`. The API's compiler errors carry no reason; the CLI adds `diagnostics` naming broken {{variable}} references.

Deletes, `version publish`, `version delete`, `environment delete`, `environment reauthorize` and `workspace bulk-update` with deletions require `--yes`. POST requests that fail with 5xx are not retried automatically; check with `list` or `version list` whether they took effect before retrying.

Every API request is written to a local JSON Lines audit log (`gtmc log dir`). `gtmc log summary --since <t> --allow-account <ids>` (or `--allow-container`) exits 1 and lists violations if anything outside the allowed scope was touched.
Output is JSON by default; `--format table` is for people. The complete, version-matched reference is `gtmc llm` (Markdown) or `gtmc llm --format json`; prefer it over any remembered command list.
